name: VDB Volume Rendering with OpenVDB/NanoVDB
definition: A GPU volume rendering technique for large, sparse datasets that uses OpenVDB for offline, fixed-rate, lossy compression on the CPU and NanoVDB for fast, low-overhead, on-the-fly decompression and sampling on the GPU. It enables rendering large volumes that exceed GPU memory by reducing memory footprint while maintaining random access patterns suitable for incoherent workloads like path tracing.
summary: VDB Volume Rendering with OpenVDB/NanoVDB enables GPU rendering of large sparse datasets by combining CPU-side lossy compression with GPU-side on-the-fly decompression to reduce memory footprint while maintaining random access.
